column2: Locks, shadowbans and limited-visibility warnings reported for engaging the wrong posts — and a witness who says the FBI told him to delete his own 4K footage. Whether or not any of it was coordinated, it decides which open-source evidence is still readable.

The routing table for the whole section: ballistics, GRAMA records, courtyard paving, aircraft, exploding-mic and Israel threads, each with its podcast lead and its X lead. Start here if you do not yet know which handle owns which question.

Proposed Law 4 would hand private citizens an FBI team, an intelligence team and full file access. Three hosts are the names most discussed for that role — this page sets out what each actually contributed.

This site's author, and a plain statement that almost nothing here originated here. It also carries the Battle Bun Brigade anthem, whose refrain — do not build a verdict with an empty hand — is the standard the rest of the site tries to hold.

The researcher who put N1098L at the centre of the case is also the man who killed the Egyptian-armada theory, citing decades-old Provo maintenance contracts. Someone who pushed the hardest aircraft claim and then refuted the second-hardest is the best evidence the plane work is not uniform conspiracy-building.

The distribution layer of the investigation — who said what, and where. Podcast hosts, X researchers and YouTube channels reaching hundreds of millions, indexed so a reader can find the GRAMA breakthrough or the ballistics deep-dive without hunting.

Twenty programs, from the largest podcast on earth to one-man research channels, mapped by what each one actually owns: ballistics guests, security interviews, foreign leads, motive. Mainstream television carried none of it.

InfoWars ran the case daily from September 10 onward and put ballistics specialists and Green Berets on live. Its host also read the ATF's "could not be identified or excluded" language as a non-match — the stronger reading is his inference, not a finding.

A former attorney worked sixteen search warrants into a minute-level timeline and found the pieces that will not fit: photos released after the suspect was already Mirandized, and a Discord message sent hours after that. His allegations, with the sealed records that would settle them named.

A decade-long TPUSA colleague said on camera there is "considerable evidence that there were state actors involved here" — and then stopped talking. He reportedly met the FBI director and the attorney general the next day, over death threats to his family.

Episode 287 is the most direct podcast treatment of the killing by any major host, from a woman who called Charlie her best friend and brother. She ran a tipline, published the SUV photographs, and became the primary target of the reported takedown campaigns.

The show ended mid-event. What is left is an archive of guests, appearances and statements from the final months — including the Tampa summit and the Virginia Tech stage six days before — and an open question about who controls it now.

He read private texts from Charlie on air, including the ones about Israel and donors. Two months before the killing he was given a TPUSA main stage to argue that case — a fact the donor-friction timeline treats as a data point in itself.

He describes a Hamptons gathering at which Kirk faced pro-Israel donor pressure. No attendee list or record of that meeting has been published, which is exactly why the claim sits here with its status marked rather than buried in a thread.

The most credentialed critic of the intelligence apparatus on this list, and the least easily dismissed as partisan. His lifelong subject — how agencies shape a narrative before the facts are in — is the exact shape of the foreign-leads dispute.

An amplification channel rather than a research one, and valuable for exactly that. Their Stew Peters episode carried the foreign-intelligence angle to an audience the analytical shows never reach, and their post is one source for the "break away from being pro-Israel" paraphrase.

He built an AI-queryable database of Charlie's own video, then used it. His ballistics deep-dive is the version of the rifle argument most people have actually seen, and his paved-crime-scene episode is among the most-watched pieces on the case.

He asks the question the forensic lanes do not: not how, but what Kirk represented and what removing him was meant to accomplish. Reaches Black and religious conservative audiences no other program on this list touches.

A left-populist host arriving at the same questions as the right-wing ones, which is why this FBI critique is hard to wave away as partisan. He interviewed Joe Kent about being told to stop, and hosted the crossover episode.

Eleven to fourteen million listeners an episode, and the case has barely touched the feed. Investigators treat him as the largest unused amplifier rather than a source — and this page is the watch-list for the episode that would change that.

An attorney who read the full confession texts on air and convened trial lawyers to argue the forensics. She was also on stage with Charlie six days before he died, and later said she and Tucker Carlson were "under serious threat."
A business operator's framework applied to a political killing: panels that put people who disagree in one room and let them argue it out. Useful when the evidence is contested rather than missing.
Frame-by-frame video work that TPUSA and Erika Kirk's legal team reportedly answered with a cease-and-desist. One of the very few independent programs to draw direct legal pressure over this case.

A former Navy SEAL and CIA contractor took the security-detail interview nobody else got. When the question is what a protective detail should have done that afternoon, this is the credentialed answer.
Multiple shows a day, an insider's map of who decides what in Washington, and no interest in letting the case fade. Read for the institutional reading, not the forensics.

The maximalist end of the device and foreign-service theories, and by far the loudest. This site records the claims with their physics rebuttals attached, because the claims travel and the corrections do not.

He put a sitting counterterrorism director on camera to say the inquiry was stopped — arguably the single most consequential interview in the case. He is also one of three names discussed for Law 4 authority.

The evacuation clock most timelines on this site are built on, plus the Google Trends graphics and the Israel-motive thesis. Used more than almost any other single researcher here, and labelled as attributed claims throughout.

Hundreds of accounts, indexed one page each: ADS-B tracks, drone sightings, crack-thump acoustics, GRAMA threads. This is where the open-source work actually happened, with every claim attributed to whoever made it.

Texas corporate filings and county deed histories for the roommate's family, posted with a question about timing. The follow-up post — showing the sale was an intra-family trust transfer — is on the page too.

Waveform panels, a crack-bang gap of 0.08 to 0.14 seconds, and a conclusion that the source was 70 to 90 feet away at ground level. The method is real physics; whether those transients are crack and bang is disputed.

An independent journalist whose threads keep surfacing at the seams — the Hamptons donor meeting, the widow's shifting timeline, the custody-versus-Discord clock. Attributed claims, tracked wherever they touch the court record.
An attorney itemised what the State actually put on the record at the preliminary hearing. Both the prosecution-side and the skeptic-side pages on this site quote her, which is unusual and useful.

The 72-hour compilation most readers met first: donor-loss texts, an emergency Zoom, and the warning message. A viral template rather than authenticated documents, and the page is explicit about which is which.
A same-day frame reading with two claims that need separating: something moving past a split second before impact, which anyone can check, and a ricochet mechanism, which video cannot establish.
An aggregation account whose screenshots became evidence — the alleged $150 million offer, the leaked texts about Ben Shapiro. Archived because they circulated widely, not because they were verified.
The reply-chain questioner who keeps asking why two separate video systems that should have recorded the surrender reportedly produced nothing at all.

The counterweight. He argues the camera set and the cumulative evidence are overwhelming, and he goes after the largest independent investigators by name. Kept here because a record with only one side is not a record.

The account behind the PETN-in-the-mic-wire video, plus the SUV glass, the Valhalla thread and the autopsy framing. Every claim on the page carries its counterargument, because the claims outrun the corrections.

The physics skeptic the device theory has to get past: a 32-gram clipped mic rockets away rather than driving a stable jet, and a PETN-class event should leave flash, smoke and torn fabric. The strongest version of the other side.

The director of the National Counterterrorism Center says the FBI shut his inquiry down before he could run his leads out. He stepped down in order to say it on the record — which is what separates this from an anonymous thread.

An arm-to-arm search found nothing. A K-9 pass found nothing. Then federal agents arrived, sent local officers back over the same ground, and a towel-wrapped rifle appeared — the reported sequence skeptics keep returning to.

A records request returned roughly fifty documents: two men warning campus police the night before, an email trying to reach Charlie, and an alert failure — with every name blacked out. The university reportedly holds more and has declined to release them.
Roughly 600,000 files went to the defense; the DNA-mixture data, ballistics scans and chain-of-custody logs reportedly did not. Critics call it volume used as concealment rather than disclosure.

The FBI director reportedly called the stairwell images "enhanced." They went out on the evening the suspect was already in custody — and critics say the morning and afternoon figures do not look like the same man.
The released rooftop clip reportedly starts at 12:23:34, with the runner already moving. The whole argument is about the seconds before that — the ones nobody has published.

Locks, shadowbans and limited-visibility warnings for engaging the wrong posts, alongside a witness reportedly told to delete his own footage. Suppression does not prove a cover-up, but it does decide what survives online.

The majority citizen finding is that the fatal event was an explosive device, and this is where that argument lives — hardware, procurement, four-channel audio, and the fragments reportedly found in the SUV.

Photographs reportedly released by Candace Owens show the inside of the vehicle that carried Charlie to hospital. Analysts point at the glass on the seat and ask what tempered glass was doing anywhere near a rifle wound.
A .30-06 round carries roughly 3,950 joules. Commentators argue the wound described publicly does not match that energy — the arithmetic that makes the government's rifle account hard to accept.

Every weapon and ballistics thread in one memo: the Mauser narrative, the ATF's "could not be identified or excluded" language, the energy mismatch, and the alternative calibers. Read it before quoting any single ballistics claim.

A US Army-contracted HADES jet reportedly flew low and slow within two miles of campus, about twenty minutes after the shot and three hours before it. If it was tasked, someone holds airborne sensor records of that afternoon.

Candace Owens called it the yellow plane. An Egyptian-registered Falcon 7X reportedly sat near Provo from September 4 and left the country in the hours around the killing, leading a cluster of foreign government jets trackers have followed for years.

The organization Charlie built, the donors who funded it, and the internal friction in the weeks before September 10. Read it alongside the motive threads; much of the reported pressure ran through here.

She called Charlie her best friend and brother, then ran the largest independent probe of his death. She also published the texts, the tipline and the SUV photographs the rest of the case now argues over.
A friend of Charlie's who put Joe Kent on camera to say the inquiry was stopped. He is also one of three names discussed for Law 4 investigator authority.
The man himself — what he built, what he changed his mind about in his final months, and who he told that he was afraid. Every other page on this site is downstream of this one.
Charged, not convicted. This is the record of what the State says it has and what independent researchers say does not fit — the DNA, the Discord messages, the Miranda clock and the photographs.

A dated timeline of Israel-related friction in Charlie's last months, with every entry labelled confirmed, evidenced, disputed or unverified. That labelling is the point; this is the thread most often argued without it.

Coverage settled on one story of how Charlie died within hours and has barely revisited it since. This section is the record of that settling — the wires, the live blogs, the panels, and what they stopped asking.

Four proposed federal laws that would force the 302s, the ballistics workup, the camera feeds, the 911 audio and the flight manifests into public view. Everything else on this site is an argument; this is the ask.
A week of sessions in Provo where the ATF ballistics, the rooftop, the autopsy and the phone evidence were finally tested under cross-examination. The day-by-day record of who said what on the stand.

The case that the charged man did not cause the death: ballistics that will not match, trajectory that will not work, timing that will not close. Presented as argument, with the counter-readings kept on the page.
Halted foreign inquiries, an ISR jet overhead, foreign phones, VIP flights and scene control. Indicators rather than proof — but they are the indicators an intelligence service leaves behind.

Search-trend claims that campus layouts, rooftops and named people were being looked up months before September 10, some reportedly from Israeli IP space. Trends data is noisy, and the page says so while laying the spikes out.

Rooftop, parking, CCTV, layout, Losee Center — the reported search strings read like a site survey, and they date to May through July 2025. The page carries the boring explanation too, because a large public campus generates traffic.

Midnight to midnight on Utah's clock: the pre-dawn aircraft picture, the camera sightings from 8:07 AM, the 12:23:30 shot, the hospital run, and the evening flights. Every line labelled reported or claimed.
No counter-snipers, no Secret Service, six campus officers and a last-minute private detail. Rooftops overlooking the stage were reportedly nobody's responsibility that afternoon.

The most aggressive aircraft claim in the case: that the HADES jet dropped and recovered drones near campus. Recorded here with its refutation attached, because the researcher who pushed it is also the one others checked.

Two federal postures at once — public statements that foreign intelligence was assisting, and an on-record claim that the counterterrorism inquiry into those same threads was shut down. Both sides are on the page.
Court restrictions, silenced witnesses and an agency that stopped speaking. The reason so much of this case is argued from screenshots is that the people who know are not permitted to talk.

A former special-operations figure says a senior CIA contact told him agency personnel were turned around at the airport by the FBI, and that the Oval Office was told and did nothing. His reported account, not a finding.
The claim is usually "no autopsy." The accurate version is harder to argue with: an autopsy appears to have happened, and the report is still not public.
Donor pressure, an Israel position that was visibly shifting, warnings he reportedly gave three people, and the geopolitics around them. Motive is where this case stops being forensic.

The most-discussed foreign service in the citizen threads, appearing across motive, phones at UVU, Egyptian jet logistics and access claims. Discussion, not a court finding — and the page is careful about the difference.

Fifty-eight days before he died, Charlie put a debate about Israel, Epstein and Mossad on his own main stage, then reportedly told Tucker Carlson to go max. The clearest dated turning point in the coalition fight.
Every person near this case, sorted by role rather than by theory — witnesses, officers, staff, family, and a dedicated cluster for the people who turned out to be distractions.
The part of this site that asks something of the reader: which bills to track, who to contact, and what to preserve. Reading is not the point; the records are.
A contractor says the courtyard pave-over was run by two men who work for the state of Utah, not by campus facilities. He did not name them publicly, and this page does not either.

Three people say Charlie told them, in his last twenty-four hours, that he thought he was about to be killed. No screenshot has been published, which is why it is the most consequential and least documented claim here.
Texts she published have Charlie writing that he was not sure he would live to see the end of this revolution. The day before he died he reportedly offered her the AmFest stage back.

An archive account whose specialty is the post that later disappears — a deleted security-firm statement, a deleted staffer post. Screenshots of deleted posts cannot be independently verified, which is exactly why someone had to keep them.

Two visual-comparison claims tying people near the case to Fort Huachuca — carpet, wall colour, a public promo photograph. Visual matches are the weakest evidence class this site tracks, and the page says so before it says anything else.
The motive checklist most readers meet as a single block: the donor break, the youth pipeline, the Gaza language. Reproduced plank by plank so each one can be checked rather than swallowed whole.

Flight-record research in the John Cullen tradition — why one aircraft waited thirty minutes at a gate, and what the Egyptian fleet transponders were doing. Ramp positions and work orders could answer these questions; argument cannot.

TPUSA's spokesman is the rare account here who is an organisational insider — source and subject at once. Text authenticity, the succession statement and the "Andrew" who reportedly received the September 9 message all run through him. No court has accused him of anything.
A citizen analyst who checks viral claims against arrival clocks, and who pushed back on the 9:24 AM contact story from inside the skeptic camp. That discipline is rarer here than the claims are.

A veteran voice who cuts across both camps: his ammunition commentary supports the exit-wound argument for a rifle, while his physics critique undercuts the exploding-mic theory. Useful precisely because he is not picking a side.
Jacket-fragment measurements argued to be too small for a .30-06 profile. It is the most falsifiable of the citizen ballistics claims — released lab documentation would settle it in an afternoon.

The donor-realignment reading of what TPUSA did after September 10, restated as attributed political interpretation rather than adopted. The page is blunt about the limit: policy reversal is not homicide.

An amplifier with insider framing — a bio reportedly listing prior TPUSA work, and the quote-tweet that carried the Joe Kent shutdown clip into the movement's own audience. Circulation, not documentation.

An automated answering account, recorded here as the fact-check layer rather than as adjudication. It is the site's clearest example of machine-generated rebuttal running in the same threads as the claim it answers.

One of the main carriers of Charlie's alleged final warnings — the compilation posts through which the kill-me quotes spread. A quote amplifier rather than a document source, and the page holds that distinction.

The raw claim inventory behind the Sam Parker profile: flight data, ballistics questions, the Israeli-IP search dates, the $150 million allegation. Every line is a post, attributed and dated, not a finding.

The section's clearest counter-example: colour-coded spreadsheets arguing most of the alleged tailing flights either never existed or happened on another continent. The site keeps it beside the claim it tries to falsify.

Six campus officers, no owned rooftops, and a hired firm that also did not control the high ground. This account's function is keeping rooftop jurisdiction framed as a police question rather than a private-security one.
A low-follower account whose single clip share moved a case debate — the Bates-stamped 6:25 PM Miranda transcript read aloud from a defense motion. The strength here is the document, not the poster.

Open questions about George Zinn's reported prior contact with the travelling group, kept specific instead of general. Zinn's obstruction admission is court record; whether anyone directed him is not.

One narrow, checkable claim: does high-frame-rate footage show fabric moving before the wound appears? That is answerable with original-resolution video and imaging expertise, which is why the site logs it despite the dispute.
